- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline after peak at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat or declining, model overestimates upward momentum — reduce forecast slope.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 2–5% in bullish sentiment periods — apply downward bias of 2–3% to 30d forecast mean.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits lag — forecast should be adjusted to align with 3–5 day lag of sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, model underestimates downward risk — add 1–2% downward buffer to forecast.
- In low sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ days), model tends to ignore downward pressure — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days.
